title: South Africa's Cape
subtitle: Ocean winds and old soils
objectives: Explain the Wine of Origin scheme

steps.title: Between two oceans
steps.body: South Africa's wine regions lie in the Western Cape, at about 34 degrees south. The climate is Mediterranean. The cold Benguela Current and the Cape Doctor, a strong south-easterly wind, cool the vineyards and keep them healthy. The soils are among the world's oldest: granite, sandstone and shale.
steps.highlight: Benguela Current and the Cape Doctor

steps.title: The districts
steps.body: Stellenbosch, near Cape Town, is the historic heart, known for Cabernet Sauvignon and blends. Paarl and Franschhoek are warmer, with Huguenot history. Swartland, to the north, is dry, with old bush vines of Chenin Blanc, Syrah and Grenache. Elgin, Walker Bay and Constantia are cool and coastal. Constantia's sweet wine was famous in the 18th century.

steps.explanation: The Cape Doctor blows from the south-east, cooling vines and blowing away disease.

steps.title: Wine of Origin
steps.body: The Wine of Origin scheme, since 1973, defines regions, districts and wards. Wines are certified with a seal on the bottle. A named grape, vintage or origin requires 85%. Producers can also make single-vineyard wines from registered sites.

steps.prompt: Match each district to its feature.
steps.explanation: The Cape's districts vary with distance from the sea.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Benguela Current and Cape Doctor cool the Western Cape
Stellenbosch, Swartland and Constantia are key districts
Wine of Origin certifies origin, grape and vintage
